description:
## Goal

Give every logical source one stable typed owner and every accepted text an immutable provenance version, while making failed compiler attempts complete into the existing dependency authority. Source replacement, definition ownership, generated callable ownership and failure ownership are one atomic boundary because no partial combination can preserve accepted source, exact derived withdrawal and diagnostics.

## Public contract

- submit_source creates a new owner. A second owner for the same function, module, struct, macro or type is a conflict even when its declaration is equivalent.
- replace_source(owner, text) is the only edit operation.
- Identical text is a no-op: retain the accepted version, allocations and generations.
- A rejected replacement leaves the entire prior accepted version current.
- Once a new source version is accepted, a failing downstream derivation withdraws its stale claims, retains exactly the observations made before failure, and owns its immutable diagnostic. Unchanged failure does no work; relevant dependency movement wakes it once.
- Atomic acceptance transfers ownership and invalidates exact derived ground; it does not eagerly lower cold functions or build products.
- Old versions remain only while exact diagnostic/artifact owners retain them.

## One authority

Use existing World definition/declaration stores and scheduler publisher/read/wait frontiers. Declaration body, references, owner and provenance form one authoritative value. ModuleId, FunctionId, TypeName and generated callable identities are typed semantic identities; filenames, spans, display labels, insertion order and raw IDs are never ownership.

Generated callable identity is semantic code/capture identity owned by its lexical definition and separated from diagnostic span. Retained old closures continue to name their old immutable denotation. Equal current denotations may reuse code identity without conflating provenance.

A completed attempt returns one typed outcome containing its actual fact/product observations plus Complete, Blocked or Failed diagnostic state. Do not add a failed-job registry, retry queue, rollback World, source snapshot mirror, winner map, domain-specific owner registry or global scan.

## Absorbed correctness contracts

- fz-kdt.24: late duplicate global functions cannot evade ownership after the first source scoped.
- fz-kdt.30: a second module owner cannot overwrite the first or shadow a lazy reserved runtime module.
- fz-kdt.32: requester-owned struct expectations withdraw exactly when explicit replacement removes them.
- fz-tfn.53: type declaration body and references publish atomically under one source owner.
- fz-tfn.45: generated callable identity remains coherent across location edits, sibling insertion/reorder, body change and retained old closures.
- fz-tfn.46: failed attempts retain actual reads, withdraw stale claims, preserve diagnostics and reawaken exactly on relevant movement.

## Required deletion

Delete implicit fresh-submit replacement; demand-time whole-code duplicate discovery; module/type overwrite paths; append-only historical requester obligations; separate type-reference mirrors; span/display-based callable identity; fatal exits that discard reads; invented producers; provisional refresh adapters; rollback/reconciliation stores; compatibility APIs and stale tests/docs.

## TDD and acceptance

At the public API prove distinct-owner conflicts, same-owner identical and changed replacement, functions/modules/types/structs/macros, lazy runtime reservation, macro-generated declarations, generated lambdas, retained old diagnostics/artifacts, Blocked then Failed, prior success then failure, shared publishers, exact repair, unchanged/unrelated zero requested-root work, and current provenance. Full relevant deterministic, semantic, product and three-door gates pass.
title: Atomically own source replacement and failed derivations
